t2i_prompt: A wide web page section drawn as an engineering blueprint on a deep navy background, inside a thin drawing-sheet border with zone letters and numbers and a small title block bottom right. A single light thin sans-serif headline spans the top. Below it, three short text columns separated by thin vertical rules; each rule continues downward as a leader line to an equipment cluster. One isometric pipe in pale blue-white hairlines runs diagonally across the lower half linking the three clusters: <CONTENT>. Numbered balloon callouts and a few dimension lines. Flat, no shading, generous negative space, no people.
signature_idea: Column dividers that keep going and become leader lines into one shared pipe drawing, so text and plant are physically connected.
strengths: calmer and more spacious than take 1; easy hierarchy
column-rule-to-leader-line device is clever and buildable in CSS/SVG
one pipe linking three users tells the 'same limits' story
close to the brand's hairline navy language
weaknesses: duplicated medical-devices paragraph shows generator glitch
equipment clusters are generic and do not differ meaningfully by industry
body text is regular weight and fairly large, reads more like slide than web
no limestone surface or steel-blue highlight to focus the eye
brand_fit_why: Navy ground, hairline isometric line art, light Geist-like headline, square corners and real negative space fit well; lacks mono figures and a single steel-blue highlight.
